question: Ticket d421051bc1f7 says 'intention and why are moved from the ticket to berths pointed to by owning_intention; gates access them via that address, not as direct ticket properties', but outline 19.14.7 reads "The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. A failure is not automatically "it broke, change it". After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed. Either way the system improves, constantly. WHY: questions about a part are answered by its intention and why against the new thing's intention and why, so a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or to its implementation plan, never a conversation about procedure (Akien, 2026-11-02). The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure. It is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome: the ticket changes, or the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Nothing passes a ticket over a red; testing a sieve is what the ticket that fixes it does. (Q#62, Akien 2026-11-02.)" (Outline assumes 'the ticket's intention and why' are directly accessible properties when gates examine failures. Ticket removes these fields from the ticket object entirely, storing them in external berths instead. Gates can no longer access them as described — they must dereference owning_intention first.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
